clue.text: Account many wrongly tried to sanction

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

indicators.note: something done wrongly is done amiss, so the letters of the next word are set out of order

explanation.surface: Somebody's account of an attempt to give official approval went badly astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges TRIED to REDIT, which follows AC and C.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit someone is to give them official approval or authorisation, which is what sanction means as a verb.

clue.text: Certainly see dawn breaking round house

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation, enclosing it
dawn breaking suggests sunrise, but here the word's letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Seeing the sun come up around a home is a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' turns DAWN into ANDW; 'round' puts it around HO, giving AND HO W. 'see' is a link: you see (find) the answer this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'and how!' is an emphatic exclamation of agreement, meaning very much so, of course.

clue.text: The nearest way to the sea

definitions.text: The nearest way to the sea

parts.words: The nearest way to the sea
parts.note: not the shortest route down to the beach but a highway running along the shoreline, as close to the water as a road gets

explanation.definitionFit: A road that follows the shore is literally the route lying closest to the sea.

clue.text: Irene may appear when he is around

indicators.note: turned around, the letters of the woman's name are rearranged into a man's name

parts.note: a woman's name, used here purely for its five letters

explanation.surface: A woman called Irene turns up whenever a certain man is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: shuffle the answer's letters and IRENE appears; equally, 'around' rearranges IRENE into the man's name. 'may appear when' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's first name, so 'he' can stand for it; it is also the name of the UK computer that picks Premium Bond winners.

clue.text: He doesn't appreciate the resort of Tangier

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, sorting the letters again, so the city's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who is not grateful for the Moroccan holiday resort of Tangier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination but is read as re-sort, rearranging TANGIER. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, someone who fails to show thanks for kindness.

clue.text: Diminish value of child bearing

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
air means bearing, manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: Having a child lowers the worth of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' suggests giving birth, but it means demeanour, AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken it or reduce its quality or worth.

clue.text: Victoria's capital prime minister

explanation.surface: The leading statesman serving Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the state capital of Victoria in Australia, and Lord Melbourne was a British premier and mentor to the young Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Sailors are often so perplexed

explanation.surface: Seamen are frequently baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors are frequently out on the ocean, and the phrase is also an idiom for being confused or bewildered.

clue.text: They are paid by formal visitors

definitions.text: They are paid by formal visitors

parts.words: They are paid by formal visitors
parts.note: not money handed over but courtesies offered, from the idiom of paying a polite call on someone

explanation.definitionFit: To pay one's regards is to make a courteous visit, so these marks of esteem are what callers 'pay'.

clue.text: Doctor again involved with point of sanitation

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the word beside it are jumbled

parts.note: E (east) is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A medic once more taking part in the matter of public hygiene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges AGAIN into AINAG, placed between DR and E. 'with' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanitation systems carry waste water away through pipes and sewers, i.e. by draining it off.

clue.text: Their function is to secure quiet in class

indicators.note: the letter for quiet goes inside the word class

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A teacher's job is to keep a class silent.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into CLASS, between the second S and the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasps are fasteners, devices whose job is to hold things fast and closed.

clue.text: High spot of getting married in a church

indicators.note: the letter for married sits inside the pair of pieces that follow

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Getting wed in church is the high point of one's life.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside A + CE. 'of getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An acme is the peak or highest point of achievement, a summit.

clue.text: Striking centre-spread that's way out

parts.note: workers who are striking are said to be out

indicators.note: the centre of a six-letter word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A magazine's eye-catching centrefold is wildly unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes RE from the middle of 'spread'; 'Striking' suggests eye-catching but means on strike, OUT. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means bizarre or unconventional, which is what the slang 'way out' expresses.

clue.text: City road

explanation.surface: A city street.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the largest city in Alaska, and a road (roadstead) is a sheltered stretch of water where ships can lie at anchor.

clue.text: Go looking for a scrap when surrounded by the enemy

indicators.note: the scrap is placed inside, encircled by the hostile party

parts.note: the enemy is the foe
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Looking for a fight while encircled by hostile forces.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG goes inside FOE: FO RAG E. 'scrap' looks like a fight, but means a rag. 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search around for food or provisions.

clue.text: Battle to get a gangleader on trial

parts.note: the leader of the word gang is its first letter
a defendant on trial is in court

explanation.surface: A fight leads to a gang boss standing trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gangleader' gives G, the leading letter of 'gang'. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 battle in which Henry V of England defeated the French.

clue.text: You won't hear a sound out of it

definitions.text: You won't hear a sound out of it

parts.words: You won't hear a sound out of it
parts.note: sounds as if something is silent, but it means being beyond the range where hearing reaches

explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is hearing range, so anything outside it cannot be heard.

clue.text: Memorial of one's death

parts.note: a marker set over a grave recording when someone died

explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone stands at the head of a grave to commemorate the person buried there.

clue.text: Not quite free to give the result of the division

indicators.note: set free, the letters break loose and regroup in a new order

explanation.surface: Not entirely liberated to report what came of a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges NOT QUITE. 'to give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, dividing one number by another produces a quotient.

clue.text: Ruin the opening?

explanation.surface: Was the first night a disaster?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's downfall is their undoing, and undoing a lock or knot is the act of opening it.

clue.text: A catch one is delighted to exhibit

explanation.surface: A good catch is something a fisherman is happy to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is a part-song much like a catch (a round for voices), and also the joy a delighted person shows.

clue.text: Emperor in vehicle waves back

indicators.note: the turned piece sits inside the word for vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: going back means the word for waves is read from right to left

parts.note: the waves is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: A ruler in his carriage rides the waves home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SEA into AES, put inside CAR: C AES AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title taken by Roman emperors, after Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Many on guard in hollow

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
taken as written
cave, Latin for beware, was schoolboy slang for keep watch, be on guard

explanation.surface: Lots of people keep watch in an empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (Latin 'beware') is old British public-school slang shouted as a warning. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Concave describes a surface that curves inwards, i.e. hollowed out.

clue.text: First paint book

explanation.surface: The first coat of paint on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is the undercoat applied before other paint, and also an elementary textbook for beginners.

clue.text: Striker held by police

parts.note: not a protesting worker taken into custody but a weapon for hitting carried by officers

explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is the club or baton a police officer carries for striking.

clue.text: A French fee that's excessive

parts.note: un is the French for a
a due is a fee or charge owed, as in membership dues

explanation.surface: A charge in France that's too high.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means more than is warranted, unjustifiably great.

clue.text: One is vertical in flight

parts.note: not a climbing aircraft but the upright part of each step in a flight of stairs

explanation.definitionFit: On a staircase the riser is the upright board between two treads.

clue.text: Not a subject needed at school

explanation.surface: Not one of the lessons a pupil needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch reigns over subjects rather than being one, and a measuring stick is standard school kit.

clue.text: Finally attains a high position

parts.note: reads as eventually reaching the top, and also as something upended so its tip is uppermost

explanation.definitionFit: To finish in some state is to arrive there at last; and with the end pointing upward a thing is literally upright.

clue.text: Where everybody goes in to sweep around the floor

definitions.text: Where everybody goes in to sweep around the floor

indicators.note: the word for everybody goes inside the cleaning implement

parts.note: a broom is what you sweep with
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone sweeps across the floor at the dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL goes inside BROOM: B ALL ROOM. The whole clue also describes the room: dancers sweep around its floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall where couples glide around a dance floor.

clue.text: Break for food in an attempt to reach agreement

indicators.note: the eating goes inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to stop for food is to eat

explanation.surface: Negotiators break for lunch while trying to strike a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: EAT goes inside TRY: TR EAT Y. 'to reach' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: It may be read twice with an expression of dismay

indicators.note: the rearranged word is written two times in a row
the word may be rearranged into another word with the same letters

explanation.surface: Something that may be read a second time with an exclamation of distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges READ into DEAR, and 'twice' repeats it. 'It' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled endearment is an old-fashioned exclamation of mild distress, like 'oh no'.
